items.headline: White House frontier-model pre-release vetting EO advances to interagency draft
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's report had the NYT scoop framing the EO as an early trial balloon with no specified legal vehicle. Today's update names the architecture: a Frontier Model Review Board co-chaired by NIST and the ODNI cyber lead, mandatory 30-day pre-release notification keyed to the AISI 32-step cyber-attack-range threshold, and explicit reliance on Defense Production Act Section 708 voluntary information-sharing rather than new APA notice-and-comment rulemaking. The shift from rumor to interagency draft circulating to OSTP, NSC, NIST, and Commerce upgrades the regulatory thread from speculative to operational. AI Policy Institute, R Street, and AI Now flagging the absent comment window as a litigation vector sets the Q3 2026 legal battlefield.

items.headline: EU AI Office and UK AISI publish joint cyber-eval reciprocity protocol
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday had no trans-Atlantic reciprocity primitive on the table. Today the EU AI Office and UK AISI sign a memorandum of cooperation establishing reciprocal recognition of cyber-capability evaluations between the AI Act Section 51 systemic-risk regime and AISI's voluntary frontier-model program, with a 90-day window for AISI TLO-range runs to satisfy EU pre-deployment requirements. Mistral, Aleph Alpha, Anthropic, and OpenAI sign on as the initial cohort with results shared in confidence to both regulators. The timing alongside the FMRB draft creates the first multilateral cyber-eval primitive and explicitly anticipates a US counter-protocol, defining the trans-Atlantic regulatory shape in a single news cycle.

items.headline: UK NHS GitHub lockdown extends to wider critical-national-infrastructure stack
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's report had the NHS lockdown as the lone sovereign-supply-chain response to Mythos. Today the UK National Cyber Security Centre extends the advisory across DWP, HMRC, and Network Rail technology estates with a rolling May-15 deadline, while HM Treasury simultaneously orders a one-week pause on new public-sector LLM coding-assistant procurements. The action set widens from a single health system to the broader CNI footprint and adds a procurement-side freeze, making this the third leg of the May regulatory wave alongside the FMRB draft and the EU-UK reciprocity memorandum. It is the first procurement pause triggered by a named frontier-model capability disclosure.

items.headline: Cerebras Systems prices IPO at $128 above range
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Cerebras had launched the IPO with a $115-$125 range and a $26.6B target valuation. Today it prints at $128, three dollars above the upper end, raising approximately $3.58B with the green-shoe taking total raise to about $4.12B and fully-diluted market cap to roughly $27.2B. It becomes the largest US tech IPO of 2026 by both raise and pricing-vs-range outperformance, and OpenAI's warrant package over roughly 33M shares prices in-the-money on listing. The +2.4% above-range margin sets a concrete floor for SambaNova, Groq, and the second-tier inference-chip cohort following behind.

items.headline: SambaNova and Groq accelerate IPO prep on the Cerebras print
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's report flagged the Cerebras IPO as a template-setter but listed no follow-on filings. Today SambaNova and Groq are reported to be accelerating S-1 confidential submissions targeting the next 60-90 days, while Tenstorrent enters late-stage talks with Hyundai and Samsung Foundry on a >$3B IPO bridge round. The second-tier accelerator cohort moves from watching to executing within 24 hours of the Cerebras print, and the structured-warrant plus frontier-lab supply-contract IPO shape is now explicitly the validation reference. This crystallizes the H2 2026 issuance pipeline for the AI-accelerator equity category.

items.headline: n8n Ni8mare CVE adds to CISA KEV catalog with Shadowserver scan
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's report introduced the n8n CVE-2026-21858 disclosure with an emphasis on the CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE path. Today CISA adds the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal-civilian remediation deadline of May 21, while Shadowserver publishes its first-week scan finding ~14,200 internet-exposed n8n instances globally with roughly 62% still unpatched. Censys and Orca confirm in-the-wild exploitation through Telegram, Discord, and GitHub webhook entry points. This is the first agentic-AI-workflow-platform CVE to enter the KEV catalog, transforming Ni8mare from a single advisory into the structural pivot for the no-code-LLM-workflow-harness vulnerability category.

items.headline: LangChain LangGraph SSRF and LiteLLM proxy auth-bypass land same day
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday closed the n8n + Flowise + LMDeploy CVE wave as the operative agentic-tooling disclosure cohort. Today adds two concurrent high-severity disclosures: LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 (CVSS 9.1) is an SSRF in the checkpoint-replay endpoint pivoting to cloud-metadata services and adjacent agent state stores, and LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188 (CVSS 8.8) is an authentication bypass in the proxy admin API enabling impersonation of arbitrary virtual-key holders. Sysdig honeypot telemetry shows exploitation within 18 hours of disclosure on both. The agentic-platform CVE wave is now disclosing at multi-vendor weekly cadence rather than monthly.

items.headline: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 ships with sandboxed-skill registry and per-tenant Mythos gating
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Claude Code sat in the standing carry as a terminal-resident agent harness alongside Codex CLI and Cursor. Today Anthropic ships Claude Code 3.0 with three structural changes: a signed and version-pinned sandboxed-skill registry, per-tenant Mythos Preview gating tied to AISI cyber-eval results behind a contractual ethics-and-misuse rider, and native sub-agent dispatch with token-budget bookkeeping. OpenAI graduates the May-1 /goal feature into a richer /agent command with explicit Plan-Apply two-phase execution and ships a per-org agent registry with FedRAMP-Moderate authorization on the same day. The dual-vendor governance-by-design landing is the explicit answer to the agentic-AI attack-surface concern raised by the n8n KEV addition and the LangGraph and LiteLLM disclosures.

items.headline: Mistral Workflows enterprise uptake hits 240 customers one week post-preview
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's report had Workflows at the public-preview baseline with the original Apr 28-30 production cohort of ASML, ABANCA, CMA-CGM, France Travail, La Banque Postale, and Moeve. Today Capgemini ships an SAP-S/4HANA general-ledger reconciliation agent across 14 customers, Atos automates sovereign-cloud KYC for French and German public-sector customers, and EDF deploys a plant-data anomaly-detection agent across 56 nuclear sites. Paid Workflows tenancy crosses 240 enterprise customers (up from ~60 at preview launch) with daily-execution count surpassing 3.4M (vs ~800K). The one-week-post-preview commercial landing surface is materially deeper than preview-day expectations and becomes the operative comparable for LangGraph and Claude Code orchestrators.

items.headline: Unsloth ships Qwen3.6-Max fine-tuning with router-only LoRA on MoE
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's local-LLM optimization category sat on the standing 2026 update wave plus the Mistral Medium 3.5 inference fix loop. Today Unsloth adds native fine-tuning for Qwen3.6-Max with 4-bit and 8-bit dynamic-bits-per-parameter QLoRA on a single H100 (80GB), and introduces a LoRA-on-MoE-router-only training mode that targets only the router weights of mixture-of-experts models. Unsloth benchmarks claim 73% of full-LoRA-on-experts accuracy at 8.4% of training-step time and 12% of peak VRAM. Router-only LoRA is a structurally new compute envelope for MoE fine-tuning rather than another incremental kernel improvement, and pairs with the Apr 28 Qwen3.6 cohort as the local-LLM training-stack Pareto movement of the week.

items.headline: Figure 03 BMW Spartanburg 14-day production-run record + Apptronik Apollo Mercedes expansion
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's Physical AI category carried the Boston Dynamics Atlas commercial production launch and Tesla Optimus Gen 3 ramp at the standing baseline. Today Figure announces a 14-day continuous 8-hour-shift run on the BMW Spartanburg X3/X5 sub-assembly line at 94.6% task-success rate and 60+ totes/hour, while Apptronik expands its Apollo deployment at Mercedes-Benz Sindelfingen from 6 to 36 units across two additional sub-assembly lines with a cited 91% MTBF improvement quarter-over-quarter. Two production-line records inside a single quarter crystallize the OEM-adopted humanoid league-table thesis with hard MTBF and task-success disclosures rather than press-release framings.
